title: Astragaloside IV ameliorates diabetic nephropathy via the TGF-β1/Smad3 pathway
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy is a leading cause of end-stage renal disease. Astragaloside IV, the major active constituent of Astragalus membranaceus, ameliorated renal fibrosis in diabetic nephropathy by inhibiting the TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling pathway. These findings support the use of Astragalus in integrative management of diabetic kidney disease.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Diabetic nephropathy affects roughly 40% of patients with diabetes. Previous reports have suggested that renin-angiotensin system inhibitors slow progression, but residual risk remains high. Traditional Chinese medicine has long used Astragalus membranaceus for edema and proteinuria.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Astragaloside IV, the major active constituent of Astragalus membranaceus, ameliorated renal fibrosis in diabetic nephropathy by inhibiting the TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling pathway. Treatment with Astragaloside IV significantly reduced proteinuria compared with the model group. Network pharmacology analysis further identified Nrf2 as a key target of Astragaloside IV in oxidative stress.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Our data indicate that Astragaloside IV exerts renoprotective effects. When combined with standard ACE inhibitor therapy, Astragalus-based formulas may complement western treatment by reducing fibrosis. Further randomized trials are warranted.
